First, we express $f(x)$ as the composite function

$$
f=ln⁡u,\,u=9x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=9.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\cdot 9 \\  & =\frac{1}{9x}\cdot 9 \\  & =\frac{9}{9x} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{9}}{\cancel{9}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$
